The Independent, 18 Nov 2026

The Asia-Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth if it is to remain stable and dynamic, Chinese President Xi Jinping told business executives gathered Wednesday in the southern Chinese technology and financial hub of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.

U.S. President Donald Trump was due to join other leaders later Wednesday for the APEC leaders’ summit, traveling from the Philippines, where he attended an annual summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

Trump's “America First” approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC’s aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone. U.S. limits on Chinese access to leading-edge American technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help to power artificial intelligence, are a constant source of strain with Beijing.

Xi and other APEC leaders called for a more open approach, without directly criticizing the U.S. shift toward protecting its own markets.

APEC summit venue showcases China's central role in trade

The summit is showcasing Shenzhen, which China has transformed in the past four decades from a fishing village into a skyscraper-studded center for export manufacturing and technology. China's ascent as the second-largest economy hinged on global investments and access to world markets as global manufacturers shifted factories overseas to tap into cheaper labor and faster-growing markets.

“China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access, but also go a step further. We will carry out reform in challenging areas such as rules, regulation, and standards,” Xi told the CEO summit, reiterating Beijing's pledges to improve conditions for global investors.

“While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said. “It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”

Xi's speech highlighted China's aim to lead industrial transformation, especially in Asia, said George Chen, partner and chair of Digital Practice at The Asia Group.

“While he didn’t say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington’s more restrictive approach,” Chen said, noting that Xi did not mention export controls, Nvidia or the U.S. directly.

Pressures lie behind the pomp and positivity over open trade

Xi faces pressure at home from slowing growth as retail spending and investment have dragged as China endures a prolonged property market slump. The economy is still growing at a rate of more than 4%, but that's mainly due to surging exports that are provoking a backlash among many of China's trading partners. China's trade surplus for this year is on track to exceed $1 trillion for a second year in a row.

Still, Trump’s emphasis on friendly relations with Xi may lead to an extension of the trade truce reached last year after a series of tariff escalations.

Friction with Washington over higher U.S. tariffs and other trade barriers is leading to realignments among other trading partners. On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met with Xi and they agreed to cut tariffs on each other’s goods. Carney has cultivated tighter economic ties with China and the European Union in response to strains in Canada’s relationship with Trump.

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told the executives of top Chinese and multinational companies that bigger economies cannot impose limits on smaller countries, and that fair and dynamic growth benefits all.

“Countries cannot impose their position, their own peculiar circumstances to countries to decide," Anwar said. "They must accept that countries must emerge, focus on trade and investments, because that would ultimately benefit their people.”

Putin takes aim at sanctions, says Asia-Pacific is vital for Russia

Russian President Vladimir Putin took aim at “instruments of economic dominance,” such as the sanctions imposed following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

“Sanctions, tariffs, and export restrictions” have “outlived their usefulness and have largely lost their intimidating effect," Putin told the CEO summit in his first in-person appearance at an APEC leaders meeting since 2017.

He highlighted his country's desire to cultivate closer economic ties with the Asia-Pacific, saying trade with the region accounts for more than half of its total trade.

Russia has submitted a bid to chair APEC in 2035, Putin said.

The 21 APEC economies account for 60% of global economic activity, half of global trade and 40% of humanity. The leaders will meet behind closed doors on Thursday, while holding meetings on the event's sidelines. That will include a first-ever “trilateral” meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi, the first such summit between those three global powers.

While APEC does not take binding decisions, it serves as a forum for building a consensus on cooperation and more open trade, Anwar, the Malaysian prime minister, said.

“The decisions we, and particularly you take today, individually and collectively, will determine whether the APEC region and the international community continue to be a source of dynamism, stability and opportunity in an increasingly uncertain world," Anwar said.

Associated Press writer Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.
